open_points.text: A surface whose reading of a body fails before it has a request to hand on
open_points.question: Does “reading ... fails” mean only an I/O or HTTP-stream failure, or also failure to decode or parse a complete body into a form, service request, or upload head?
options: Only transport or framed-stream failures close the connection without an answer; syntactically invalid complete bodies produce a refusal.
Every failure before a request object exists, including decoding and multipart or form parsing, closes the connection without an answer.
open_points.default_guess: Treat transport and framed-stream failures as answerless connection closures, and treat a fully received but syntactically invalid body as a rendered refusal.

witness.initial: A valid authenticated owner session sends a request whose framing headers are accepted and whose complete body contains a malformed multipart upload head.
events: instance_lifecycle accepts the headers and dispatches the request to the owner surface.
The owner surface receives all body bytes but cannot parse the upload head into a request.
outcomes: The parsing failure counts as body-reading failure, so nothing is answered and the connection is closed.
The body was read successfully and only request decoding failed, so the owner interface renders a malformed-request refusal.
witness.observer: The owner’s HTTP client sees either an empty closed connection or a refusal response.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:Status: Status — changed since its latest review
open_points.text: A surface whose reading of a body fails before it has a request to hand on — a form, a service request, an upload's head
open_points.question: Which named module capability reads each body or upload head and detects this failure before handing a request to operations?
options: Separate request-reading capabilities of service_api and owner_interface.
A per-request body-reading capability of instance_lifecycle.
A decoding capability invoked by operations after the surface hands it the body stream.
open_points.default_guess: Give service_api and owner_interface explicit request-reading capabilities; keep HTTP framing in instance_lifecycle and domain operations in operations.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:Status: Status — changed since its latest review
open_points.text: Once an upload's file part is handed on, its stream's failure is migration_import's file_unreadable
open_points.question: Who hands the file stream to migration_import, and through which capability, while preserving operations’ stage-(1) owner-session and CSRF checks?
options: owner_interface hands the stream to operations, which invokes migration_import after stage (1).
owner_interface invokes migration_import directly after separately obtaining admission from operations.
owner_interface hands the stream directly to migration_import, which calls back through operations for admission.
open_points.default_guess: owner_interface should hand the upload request and stream to operations; operations should complete stage (1) and then invoke migration_import.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:Status: Status — changed since its latest review
open_points.question: Which module owns closing the per-request connection, what capability performs it, and who calls that capability after an early body failure or after rendering file_unreadable?
options: instance_lifecycle exposes a connection-close capability called by each surface.
The surface owns the accepted connection and closes it directly.
The surface returns a close-after-response result that instance_lifecycle applies.
open_points.default_guess: Have each surface return an explicit close-without-response or close-after-response result, applied by instance_lifecycle, which owns the listeners and connections.
